quality_summaries:
Judge 1 verdict: neither version wins across the board. I prefer Y for all four U1 (ogre) animations and for the U3 flinch. I prefer X for the U2 (swordsman) strike, flinch and death and for the U3 (demon) idle, strike and death. The U2 idles are pixel-identical, so that is a tie.

How I checked: I sampled each 3x frame back to 160x128 and compared it pixel by pixel with frame 0 and with the other version. I also looked for magenta and stray specks, checked where the feet touch the ground, overlaid the frame-0 outline on every frame, and zoomed in.

- **Idles:** each version has one idle that is effectively frozen. U1 X changes by only about 80 pixels (a fist flicker) and U3 Y by about 100 (flame-tip pixels). The other idles show a real breath.
- **Strike direction:** U2 and U3 face right in their idles. X strikes to the right, toward that facing, with a strong lunge. Y always strikes to the screen-left, on the weapon side, so the character turns his head away to land the blow.
- **X's main problems:** the blade is cut off by the frame edge on U3's swing and hit frames, and U1's lying death frames are a muddled tangle with magenta specks.
- **Problems in both:** U2 is drawn 10-20% larger than his idle in the middle frames, worse in Y. The death in every unit jumps from kneeling forward straight to lying on the back. Weapons are cut off at the top edge in several raised-weapon frames.

Overall I slightly prefer Y. Y wins 7 animations (all of U1, and U3's strike, flinch and death), X wins 4 (U3 idle, and U2's strike, flinch and death), and U2 idle is a tie because the two versions are pixel-identical.

1. **Facing on the strike.** Each version reverses facing on one unit's strike. Y's U2 swordsman faces lower-right at rest but turns and slashes left. X's U3 demon faces left at rest but spins and slashes right, and the frame edge also cuts off the sword on the HIT frame.
2. **Idles.** Both versions have one dead idle. X's U1 idle is almost static, with only a claw flicker on frame 2. Y's U3 idle is static apart from a flicker on the sword's flame edge.
3. **U1 strike.** Y has the better impact: the club reaches the ground on the HIT frame and the front foot steps in. In X the club is still at waist height on the hit and the body slides about 20px backward.
4. **Clean-up in U1.** X has more artifacts: magenta specks in the hair, a smeared pink club handle in the death, and muddier lying frames.
5. **X's strengths.** X has the stronger knock-back flinch and the better death on U2. X's U3 flinch and death, however, turn the demon squat and chibi-like, and the dropped sword shrinks.
6. **Shared problems.** On U1 and U3, both versions often let the frame edge cut off the weapon on the raised and swinging frames.

All crops and zooms are in /tmp/judge2_pairsY. My early split.py and stats.py also went into /tmp/judge2, which already held another judge's files. I did not open those files.

JOINTS: I made the weapon hand (r_) the screen-left fist, which grips the end of the hoe shaft. Final joints:
- head 74,62; neck 74,71; chest 73,78; pelvis 72,87

- l_sh 82,73; l_el 87,86; l_ha 89,99

STRIKE DIRECTION: The guides strike where the worker looks.

FRAME-0 FIT: I diffed cell 1 against the plain sprite. Only 41 canvas px of red tint fall off the sprite: the left foot, above the hat crown and right of the face. After I nudged r_ft, r_kn and head, it was 33 px.

OTHER CLAIMS CHECKED: The recipe refuses a unit file without facing, and one with a missing joint, with the messages the guide implies.

findings.doc_quote: The sprite. An M7 unit PNG ... holding one weapon in one hand. ... | lower-right | left (the near hand) | near set ... | lower-right | right (the far hand) | far set, mirrored |
findings.evidence: The worker holds the hoe in BOTH hands: the screen-left fist is at about (64,85) on the end of the shaft, and the screen-right fist is at about (89,99) lower down. The guide never says which one is the weapon hand, and the choice changes everything. With the screen-left hand, --show-beats says 'pose set near' and the guide hoe runs the full ~50 px. With the screen-right hand, it says 'pose set far (mirrored)', the strike is different, and the hoe guide is a ~21 px stub (89,99 to 106,112). In both sets the free hand lets go: strike 2 has the 'left fist tucked across the belly' and strike 4 has the 'left arm swung back', so the model will be asked to swing a two-handed tool with one hand. The hands key has no example for a weapon held in both hands.
findings.fix: Add under 'The sprite' / joints: 'Two-handed weapons (hoe, spear, polearm): use the hand at the END of the shaft, farthest from the weapon's head, as the weapon hand (r_), so r_ha to tip runs along the whole weapon; the other hand is l_. The poses swing one-handed, so in hands say that the other hand holds the shaft at rest and lets go during the swing (e.g. "... his left hand holds the shaft lower down at rest and is an empty fist when it lets go").' Also add a worked example or a table row for this case.

findings.doc_quote: The defaults already point the right way for your unit's facing.
findings.evidence: The guide never tells you to compare each beat text from 1d with its guide cell from 1e, and for the worker they disagree. Strike 1's default text says 'the sword is lifted beside the head with the tip pointing up and back'. The worker's strike 1 blockout instead raises the hoe over the head pointing FORWARD: the hand is at about canvas (54,45) and the weapon runs right and slightly down to about (105,62). This happens because the hoe rests pointing down-right, and the retarget keeps that angle until the source bone has 'turned well away from rest'. The model would get a text and a blockout that point opposite ways. I kept the text's direction, as 1d says, so my override has the same contradiction.
findings.fix: Add to 1e: 'Read every guide cell against its beat text from 1d. If your weapon rests at a different angle from the swordsman's (pointing down like a hoe, or on the shoulder like a club), early frames such as strike 1 may hold the weapon differently from the text. Then reword that text to describe what the guide shows. Where they disagree, the text is what you change, not the direction of the strike.'

findings.doc_quote: | `head_r` | head radius in px (the swordsman's is 13) | ... Row 1 starts with the frame-0 blockout laid over the sprite in a red tint: limbs, head and weapon should lie on the sprite's.
findings.evidence: head_r barely affects the guides. I ran --check-guides with head_r 5, 9 and 13. Going from 9 to 5 changed 340 pixels of the 2240×768 sheet, and from 9 to 13 changed 5604. The large dark 'hair' cap on every blockout head looked the same in all three runs. In the frame-0 overlay, the head blob spans canvas x 60–88 and y 47–68 (about 27 px), while the worker's face is about 18 px wide. Part of the blob sits on the hat crown, and head_r cannot make the head line up. The guide also doesn't say that the grey guides draw hair on every head, even on a unit with a hat.
findings.fix: Say what head_r actually controls: 'head_r sets only the face disc; the dark hair cap is drawn at a fixed size, so a small or hatted head will look too big in the overlay. That is expected, and the description carries the hat or hair.' Alternatively, make head_r (or scale) size the cap.

findings.doc_quote: Open `work/final_<unit>/guides_check.png`. Row 1 starts with the frame-0 blockout laid over the sprite in a red tint: limbs, head and weapon should lie on the sprite's. The rest of row 1 is the strike poses ..., row 2 the flinch and row 3 the death.
findings.evidence: The tint is too faint to judge by eye. It turns a background pixel from (126,170,60) to (151,110,66), and on the sprite it shows only as a slight pink cast on the white sleeves and purple on the blue cloth. At the PNG's native size (cell 1 is at 2×) I could not see it at all. Even at 6× I could not trace individual limbs, so I had to diff cell 1 against the plain sprite to see the blockout. guides_check.png has no grid, no coordinates and no frame labels, so a misplaced limb cannot be read back as canvas coordinates to fix the joint.
findings.fix: Say: 'Cell 1 is at 2×: zoom it to 4× or more. The tint is faint: look for any tint on the background, which means a blockout part is off the sprite, and for pink or purple on the clothes. Row 1 after the overlay is strike 1–6, row 2 is flinch 0–2, row 3 is death 1–7.' Better: draw the frame-0 blockout as an outline over the grid image.

findings.doc_quote: If it warns that the guide weapon was shortened, the weapon is too long for the 160×128 canvas in those frames: the model will draw it full length and it will be cut off at the edge (see Known limits).
findings.evidence: For the worker it warned for strike 2, strike 5 and death 3. In strike 2 the clamp is the left edge: the guide hoe reaches x 17. In strike 5 and death 3 the clamp is the bottom: the guide hoe reaches y 125.5 and 126.5, which is the feet line. A full-length hoe there would go through the floor, not off the side. The guide also gives no action: should I carry on, move tip, or shorten the weapon? Known limits only says that changing the canvas is untested.
findings.fix: Add: 'You need not fix this: carry on, and in step 3 reject variants where the weapon is cropped. Do not move tip to make the warning go away; it must stay on the real weapon. A clamp at the bottom means the full weapon would reach below the feet; the beat text ("nearly touches the ground") is what keeps the model from drawing it there.'

findings.doc_quote: | `scale` | the figure's height ÷ 86 (the swordsman's), measured from the top of the head or hair (not horns, hat or weapon) to the soles; e.g. 98 px → 1.14.
findings.evidence: The worker's straw hat (crown at canvas y 44, brim at y 55–59) hides the top of his head, so the top of the head and hair cannot be seen. I estimated it at y ≈ 53 by assuming the eye (y ≈ 62) is halfway down the head and the chin is at y ≈ 70. With the soles at y 125 that gives 72 px, so scale 0.84. The guide gives no rule for this case.
findings.fix: Add: 'If a hat or helmet hides the top of the head, estimate it: the top of the head is about as far above the eyes as the chin is below them.'

findings.doc_quote: | `tip` | the weapon's far end (blade tip or club head), wherever it rests, even over the shoulder |
findings.evidence: A hoe's iron blade hangs at right angles to the shaft, so its 'far end' could be where the shaft meets the head (about 106,112) or the bottom of the blade edge (about 99,123). The two give r_ha to tip angles about 12° apart. I chose the shaft-meets-head point.
findings.fix: Add: 'For a tool whose head sits across the shaft (hoe, axe, hammer, pick), put tip where the shaft meets the head, so r_ha to tip runs along the shaft.'

findings.doc_quote: Check that the strike reaches toward the unit's facing, and fix the joints until frame 0 lines up and no pose looks broken.
findings.evidence: In death 4–7 the loose weapon at the lower-right is drawn as a sword with a crossguard and hilt, even though the worker carries a hoe and every override says 'hoe'. A reader checking that 'no pose looks broken' cannot tell whether this is a defect to fix in the joints, which it is not, or something that is expected.
findings.fix: Add to 1e: 'In death 4–7 the dropped weapon is always drawn as a generic sword. That is expected; the beat texts for death 4–7 must name your weapon so the model draws it instead.'

findings.doc_quote: Override every text that names a prop your unit does not have (a club instead of a sword, an empty fist or a cape instead of a shield), as a string keyed by frame number: "beats": {"strike": {"2": "...", "4": "..."}, "flinch": {"0": "..."}, "death": {"5": "..."}}
findings.evidence: For the worker, --show-beats flagged 15 of the 16 texts: every one except flinch 2. The example, with 5 keys, suggests a few overrides. A hoe has an iron 'blade', so it is unclear whether [blade]-flagged texts can stay. Strike 5 also says 'hair trailing back', which doesn't suit a unit in a hat, and only props are flagged. After overriding, the marker column shows 'own', which the guide never explains.
findings.fix: Say: 'For a unit without a sword and shield, expect to override almost every text (the worker: 15 of 16). Also reword other features the unit lacks (hair under a hat, a cape). Your overrides are marked "own".' The guide also has no rewording example for a non-sword, lower-right unit, which it could add.

findings.doc_quote: This prints the facing, the pose set, and the text each sheet cell will get ... / plus a smear arc and an impact spark on the strike when the weapon is a steel-coloured blade (other weapons get no strike effects)
findings.evidence: --show-beats also printed 'smear cw', which the guide never explains. The guide also doesn't say how the recipe decides whether a weapon is a 'steel-coloured blade', or whether the worker's grey iron hoe blade will get the smear and spark. The only hint is 'smear cw', which suggests it will.
findings.fix: Explain 'smear cw/ccw' in 1d, say how the steel-blade test is made (and whether a unit file can turn the effects on or off), and say whether a grey tool head such as a hoe or axe counts.

findings.doc_quote: | `sprite` | path from the project root, e.g. `"m7/roster/units/unit_ogre_embers.png"` |
findings.evidence: 'Project root' could mean the repository root, which the guide itself calls the root (`CLAUDE.md`), or projects/ffh-anim-sprint/. The example and the behaviour show it is the latter: with the unit file in /tmp, the path was resolved against projects/ffh-anim-sprint, the working directory.
findings.fix: Say: 'path relative to projects/ffh-anim-sprint/ (where you run the commands), e.g. ...'.

findings.doc_quote: - VERIFY-PLACEHOLDER
findings.evidence: Line 315, in 'After the sprint', is a placeholder that was left in the published guide.
findings.fix: Replace it with the finding it stands for, or delete the bullet.

_about: Post-rule verification round A, on sets generated with a prompt bug (the per-cell facing sentence was sent unformatted). Direction: 3 blind judges over six sets (letters in key.direction). Quality: 3 blind judges, old vs new per unit (key.pairs), rubric motion 35 / consistency 30 / style 20 / appeal 15, weighted scores per judge. It found Hyborem looks lower-left, not lower-right as first assumed. doc and dry: the doc fact-check and the cold dry run on the worker.
